definition: Portent means a sign taken to foretell something, usually something bad.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word portent. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know portent should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The harbormaster read the oily green light on the horizon as a portent and ordered every small boat back inside the breakwater.
A hint is milder than a portent — a nudge that something may be so, with none of the portent's weight of approaching trouble.
A death knell is stronger than a portent — a portent warns that trouble may be coming, while the knell announces that the end has already arrived.

An omen is any sign read as a message about the future, and an omen can promise luck as easily as ruin. A portent has lost that neutrality: it leans toward trouble, the storm and the collapse, which is why histories reach for it when dread is the point.

A warning is a direct alert that someone deliberately gives — spoken, posted, or sounded — with nothing mystical about it. A portent is not given by anyone: it is a mute sign in the world itself, which observers read as pointing toward trouble still on its way.

An augury is the act or art of reading signs — Roman priests took auguries from the flight of birds — so the word names the interpretation. A portent is the sign itself, the thing being read, and it usually arrives already shadowed with coming trouble.

For three days before the quake, the valley behaved strangely.
Dogs would not settle, the well water turned cloudy, and on the second evening thousands of starlings rose off the ridge at once and did not come back.
The old surveyor wrote later that he had read the empty ridge as a portent, a mute sign that something under the valley was about to give.
He told no one at the time; there was nothing official to report, only a feeling with feathers and cloudy water behind it.
When the ground finally buckled that Friday, the starlings were forty miles away, and the surveyor's notebook became the most quoted page in the county.
